<a id="ascii-ui-layouts"></a>

# ASCII UI Layouts

An ASCII UI layout is a small text specification rendered into a text wireframe at a locked layout block. It is a sketch tool for structure and flow, not a pixel editor.

`asciiui add --book <book> --parent <node> --file <spec>` creates the locked block and stores the spec; `asciiui set --block <block> --file <spec>` replaces the spec; `asciiui remove --block <block>` deletes both. The spec travels with the book in the container.

A spec is an indented tree with two spaces per level, and `#` starts a comment. The optional `title` line sets the frame title, and `legend true` appends the generated legend.

The node kinds are `panel`, `row`, `col`, `button`, `label`, `input`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `list`, `image`, `value` and `separator`. A `row` places its children side by side; a `col` and a `panel` stack them; a `panel` draws a frame.

The words after a kind form its label, and `widget=` overrides the type of one node. A `list` accepts a trailing count, and a `separator` fills the panel width.

```text
panel Menu
  button Save
  button Cancel
```

```text
+------------+
| Menu       |
| [ Save ]   |
| [ Cancel ] |
+------------+
```

Frames stretch to the row height, stacked panels share a width, rows join with two spaces, and the drawing is emitted as a fenced text block at the block's placement.

Defaults are generic names. `asciiui.types` in the project configuration names the project type for a kind and wins over a generic explicit label; a non-generic `widget=` stays a one-node override. `widget=` names a UI widget type, never a content or domain object.

A spec is parsed before it is stored: an unknown widget or malformed indentation is rejected with a stable code. The layout block is locked, so the editor refuses its body; change the spec through the command.

Limits: list entries are placeholders (`- item N`), there are no widths or styles, and the output is plain text. Use the block for structure sketches, not for final screens.
